final_native_object_if_different.title: Uniform-field dielectric sphere: candidate solution and its class
final_native_object_if_different.statement:
Let the laboratory frame and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], with spatial coordinates $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, $z=x_3$, $r=|x|$ and the applied field along $e_3$. Fix $a>0$, a field magnitude $E_0>0$ and constants $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\in(0,\infty)$ (the interior and exterior permittivities of the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]], the material being at rest in the laboratory frame), and put $$C:=\frac{3\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}},\qquad d:=\frac{E_0a^3(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}})}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}.$$ Consider the time-independent potentials $$\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}(x):=-C\,E_0\,z\quad(r<a),\qquad \varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x):=-E_0\,z+\frac{d\,z}{r^3}\quad(r>a),$$ with fields $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ and $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}E$ inside, $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}E$ outside ($E$ being of the class of [[def-em-fields]] restricted to this time-independent configuration). Write $S=\{r=a\}$ and $n=e_r$ for the outward normal. Then:
(a) [Harmonicity] $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ on $r<a$ and $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ on $r>a$ in the classical sense of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and the potentials and their first derivatives extend continuously to the closed sides of $S$.
(b) [Interface conditions] With one-sided traces at $r=a$, $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $S$; equivalently the tangential field is continuous and the normal component of $D$ is continuous, so the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] hold along $S$ in the time-independent reading with $\sigma_f=0$.
(c) [Asymptotics] $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x)+E_0z=dz/r^3$ and $\nabla(\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z)=O(r^{-3})$ as $r\to\infty$: the difference from the applied uniform potential decays like $r^{-2}$ and its gradient like $r^{-3}$.
(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] Let $(\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}},\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}})$ be $C^2$ on the closed ball $\overline{B_a}$ respectively on every closed exterior region $\{a\le r\le R\}$, harmonic on $r<a$ and $r>a$, satisfying the same interface conditions (b), and satisfying $|\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z|\le M/r$ for some $M$ and all sufficiently large $r$. Then $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$. Hence the displayed pair is the unique solution of the dielectric-sphere transmission problem in that class, existence being exhibited explicitly; the uniqueness proof uses only the Green identity, the matching conditions and the decay, with no maximum principle.
(e) [Fields, polarisation and induced dipole] On $r<a$ the field is uniform, $E=C E_0e_3$ with $D=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}CE_0e_3$; outside, the field is that of the applied uniform field plus the field of a point dipole at the origin with moment $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,d\,e_3$; the interior polarisation is $P_{\mathrm{in}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_0)CE_0e_3$ and the bound surface charge density on $S$ is $\sigma_b=n\cdot(P_{\mathrm{in}}-P_{\mathrm{out}})$, the singular coefficient of $\rho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$ at $S$ (with the exterior polarisation $P_{\mathrm{out}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}-\varepsilon_0)E_{\mathrm{out}}$).
(f) [Regime and scope] The computation is a quasistatic result of the declared linear branch at $\sigma_f=0$; using $p$ as a dynamic wave polarisability of the sphere requires a separate quasistatic/dipole approximation and is not asserted here. The example asserts no material data and no empirical claim.

**Proof technique:** explicit substitution plus a maximum-principle/Green-identity uniqueness argument. (a): $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ is linear and $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=-E_0z+d z/r^3$; the second partials are computed with [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], giving $\Delta z=0$, $\Delta(r^{-3})=6r^{-5}$ and hence $\Delta(d z/r^3)=d(z\cdot6r^{-5}+2(-3z r^{-5}))=0$ by the product rule; both sides extend smoothly to $r=a$ from their own side. (b): evaluate $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}(a)=-CE_0a\cos	heta$ and $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(a)=(-E_0a+d/a^2)\cos	heta$, whose equality is $C=1-d/(E_0a^3)$; the radial derivatives are $-CE_0\cos	heta$ and $(-E_0-2d/a^3)\cos	heta$, whose equality after weighting by $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}$ is $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}C=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}(1+2d/(E_0a^3))$. The linear system has determinant $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ and the displayed solution, so the interface equations hold; the equivalence with the jump conditions uses $E=-
abla\varphi$, $D=\varepsilon E$ and [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with $\sigma_f=0$. (c) is immediate from $|z|\le r$. (d): the difference $(w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}})$ is harmonic on each side with matching traces $f=	ilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}-\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ on $S$ and flux continuity $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{out}}$, and $|w_{\mathrm{out}}|\le(M+|d|)/r	o0$ uniformly. Apply the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] to $u=v=w_{\mathrm{in}}$ on the ball and to $u=v=w_{\mathrm{out}}$ on the annulus $\{a<r<R\}$ (both are bounded C^1 domains and the functions are $C^2$ up to the boundary): since $\Delta w=0$, this gives $\int_{B_a}|
abla w_{\mathrm{in}}|^2=\oint_S w_{\mathrm{in}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\int_{a<r<R}|
abla w_{\mathrm{out}}|^2=\oint_{\{r=R\}}w_{\mathrm{out}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{out}}-\oint_S w_{\mathrm{out}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{out}}$, all with the outward normal of the respective domain. Multiply the first by $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}$ and the second by $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}$ and add: the two surface terms on $S$ cancel by $w_{\mathrm{in}}=w_{\mathrm{out}}=f$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\partial_rw_{\mathrm{out}}$, while the term on $\{r=R\}$ tends to $0$ as $R	o\infty$ by $|w_{\mathrm{out}}|=O(R^{-1})$ and $|
abla w_{\mathrm{out}}|=O(R^{-2})$ ([[cor-harmonic-cauchy-estimates-in-supremum-norm]] on balls of radius $R/2$). Since $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}>0$, both gradients vanish, so $w_{\mathrm{in}}$ (on the ball) and $w_{\mathrm{out}}$ (on $\{r>a\}$) are constant; $w_{\mathrm{out}}	o0$ at infinity forces $w_{\mathrm{out}}=0$, hence the common trace $f=0$, and then $w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ by uniqueness for the classical Dirichlet problem [[cor-classical-dirichlet-and-poisson-problems-are-unique]](1) applied on the ball to $w_{\mathrm{in}}$ and the zero function. $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is carried from the Green-identity and Dirichlet-uniqueness suppliers. (e): $E_{\mathrm{in}}=-
abla\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=CE_0e_3$; the exterior potential is the uniform potential plus the standard dipole term $p\cdot x/(4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}r^3)$ with $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}d\,e_3$, and the bound surface charge is the singular coefficient $-n\cdot[P]$ of $ho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$, with the one-sided polarisations from $D=\varepsilon E$. (f) records the regime. No empirical premise and no material data are used.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Electromagnetism (University of Texas at Austin course), node 71: Boundary value problems with dielectrics
references.locator: node 71, second example: the dielectric sphere of radius $a$ and dielectric constant $\epsilon$ in a uniform $z$-directed field, with the potentials $-E_0r\cos\theta+E_0\alpha a^3\cos\theta/r^2$ outside and $-E_1r\cos\theta$ inside, the matching conditions (835), (838)-(841), and the bound surface charge (842); read in the retained offline full text of the course.

references.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall 1999, 596 pp.; full scanned text)
references.locator: §4.4.2 printed pp. 186-188, Example 4.7: 'A sphere of homogeneous linear dielectric material is placed in an otherwise uniform electric field $\mathbf E_0$', solved by the same potentials with the boundary conditions $V_{\rm in}=V_{\rm out}$ and $\epsilon\,\partial V_{\rm in}/\partial r=\epsilon_0\,\partial V_{\rm out}/\partial r$ (no free charge); read in the stamped 596-page scan.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 printing, 236 pp.)
references.locator: §7.1.2 printed pp. 176-178 (PDF pp. 184-186), the dielectric-sphere example with a charge at the centre: the modified Gauss law determines $\mathbf D$ directly and the bound surface charge produces the field discontinuity; used here only as the source's companion illustration of the same interface structure. Read in the retained 236-page full text.

final_native_object_if_different.physical_scope: The explicit uniform-field dielectric-sphere candidate of the quasistatic linear branch: the two harmonic potentials, their matching at $r=a$ with $\sigma_f=0$, the $O(r^{-2})$ decay of the difference from the applied uniform potential, uniqueness in the declared decay class, the uniform interior field $C E_0e_3$, the exterior dipole moment $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}d\,e_3$ and the bound surface charge. Conditional on the declared constants and interface hypotheses; no dynamic polarisability, no material data and no empirical claim.
